questions.stem: At a compliance-versus-system audit decision, a supervisor proposes: "Interviews alone can establish criteria after conclusions are written". The underlying case is: An audit team begins interviews without defining which standards, locations, processes, or time period will be evaluated. What is the primary risk? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: The audit will automatically cover every legal and voluntary requirement
Undefined scope guarantees greater auditor independence
Findings may be inconsistent or indefensible because scope and criteria were not established before evidence collection
Interviews alone can establish criteria after conclusions are written
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Audit scope and criteria frame evidence needs and conclusions. They should be agreed and documented before fieldwork, with justified adjustments recorded.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'The audit will automatically cover every legal and voluntary requirement' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling audit criteria and scope principle.
The proposed response 'Undefined scope guarantees greater auditor independence' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling audit criteria and scope principle.
The proposed response 'Interviews alone can establish criteria after conclusions are written' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling audit criteria and scope principle.

questions.stem: At a closing conference, a supervisor proposes: "Accept management’s statement because position determines reliability". The underlying case is: A manager states that inspections occur weekly, but no records exist and employees describe irregular inspections. How should the auditor report this? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Accept management’s statement because position determines reliability
Create missing inspection records so the program can be evaluated
Assume employee recollections are always conclusive without sampling records
Base the finding on corroborated evidence and note the inconsistency rather than accepting assertion alone
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Auditors use verifiable evidence from documents, interviews, and observation. Conflicts should be investigated and reported objectively.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Accept management’s statement because position determines reliability' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling objective evidence principle.
The proposed response 'Create missing inspection records so the program can be evaluated' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling objective evidence principle.
The proposed response 'Assume employee recollections are always conclusive without sampling records' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling objective evidence principle.

questions.stem: At an audit-program risk assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Convenience sampling is always statistically random". The underlying case is: A corporate audit samples only the newest and best-performing site because it is easiest to visit. What weakness does this create? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Selection bias can produce an unrepresentative conclusion about the broader audit population
Convenience sampling is always statistically random
Sampling one site proves every site conforms when procedures are corporate
The best-performing site should be excluded from all audits
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Risk-based or representative sampling should reflect the audit objective. Convenience selection can systematically miss important conditions.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Convenience sampling is always statistically random' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling sampling risk principle.
The proposed response 'Sampling one site proves every site conforms when procedures are corporate' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling sampling risk principle.
The proposed response 'The best-performing site should be excluded from all audits' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling sampling risk principle.

questions.stem: At an opening audit meeting, a supervisor proposes: "Independence matters only in financial audits". The underlying case is: A manager is assigned to audit the corrective-action system that the manager designed, operates, and reports as successful. What concern should be addressed? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Self-audit is prohibited in every circumstance regardless of safeguards
Objectivity may be impaired, so independent review or safeguards should be used
Independence matters only in financial audits
Technical familiarity automatically eliminates all bias
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Auditors should be sufficiently objective and free from self-review threats. Expertise can help, but it does not remove the need for impartiality.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Self-audit is prohibited in every circumstance regardless of safeguards' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling auditor independence principle.
The proposed response 'Independence matters only in financial audits' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling auditor independence principle.
The proposed response 'Technical familiarity automatically eliminates all bias' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling auditor independence principle.

questions.stem: At an evidence-sampling plan, a supervisor proposes: "Every paperwork issue must be ranked above a physical hazard". The underlying case is: An auditor observes a missing signature on one low-risk form and a systemic failure to control hazardous energy. Why should findings not be classified solely by count? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Every paperwork issue must be ranked above a physical hazard
All findings should receive identical priority to avoid judgment
Classification should reflect significance, systemic nature, consequence, and requirement—not the number of examples alone
Only the oldest finding can be considered major
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: One systemic high-consequence breakdown can be more significant than many minor documentation lapses. Classification needs defined risk and system criteria.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Every paperwork issue must be ranked above a physical hazard' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling finding classification principle.
The proposed response 'All findings should receive identical priority to avoid judgment' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling finding classification principle.
The proposed response 'Only the oldest finding can be considered major' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling finding classification principle.

questions.stem: At a finding-classification discussion, a supervisor proposes: "Whether the finding can be renamed so it is not considered recurring". The underlying case is: A recurring audit finding is repeatedly closed by retraining employees, but procedures and equipment remain confusing. What should the follow-up examine? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Whether the finding can be renamed so it is not considered recurring
Whether the next audit can omit the area to avoid duplication
Whether training attendance sheets contain more signatures
Whether the corrective action addressed underlying process, design, ownership, and verification weaknesses rather than symptoms
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Recurring findings indicate ineffective corrective action or deeper systemic causes. Follow-up should test risk reduction, not administrative closure.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Whether the finding can be renamed so it is not considered recurring' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling root cause of audit finding principle.
The proposed response 'Whether the next audit can omit the area to avoid duplication' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling root cause of audit finding principle.
The proposed response 'Whether training attendance sheets contain more signatures' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling root cause of audit finding principle.

questions.stem: At a corrective-action follow-up, a supervisor proposes: "Avoid identifying criteria because standards can be interpreted differently". The underlying case is: During the closing meeting, site leaders dispute a finding because they first see the evidence and criteria in the final slide. What practice would have improved the audit? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Discuss factual observations and emerging concerns during fieldwork, then present evidence, criteria, significance, and next steps clearly at closing
Avoid identifying criteria because standards can be interpreted differently
Negotiate away any disputed finding regardless of evidence
Withhold all concerns until the final report to surprise management
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: No-surprise communication allows factual correction while preserving auditor judgment. Findings should be traceable to evidence and criteria.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Avoid identifying criteria because standards can be interpreted differently' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling closing meeting communication principle.
The proposed response 'Negotiate away any disputed finding regardless of evidence' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling closing meeting communication principle.
The proposed response 'Withhold all concerns until the final report to surprise management' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling closing meeting communication principle.

questions.stem: At an auditor independence review, a supervisor proposes: "Audit only sites that volunteer because they are easiest to coordinate". The underlying case is: A three-year audit schedule treats every site identically despite major differences in hazard, change, past performance, and legal exposure. What improvement is best? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Eliminate periodic review of the audit program itself
Use a risk-based audit program that adjusts frequency, scope, competence, and methods using site and system information
Audit only sites that volunteer because they are easiest to coordinate
Use the longest interval for high-hazard sites to reduce disruption
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Audit resources should be directed by risk, change, previous results, and strategic importance while maintaining appropriate coverage and independence.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The proposed response 'Eliminate periodic review of the audit program itself' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling audit program risk management principle.
The proposed response 'Audit only sites that volunteer because they are easiest to coordinate' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling audit program risk management principle.
The proposed response 'Use the longest interval for high-hazard sites to reduce disruption' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling audit program risk management principle.
